From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 29 Oct 2025 00:10:00 +09:00
Subject: Fwd: Intro / demo — some slot options (Tokyo/Singapore)

Lauren — forwarding Mina's note. Looks like the invite was created in my calendar (Redwood) but the event timezone metadata may have been left as PDT when you created it from your client, which can cause clients to display the local equivalent (hence Mina saw 00:30 on Nov 6).

Two quick things to avoid the next-day confusion:
1) Create the invite and explicitly set the event timezone to "Asia/Tokyo" rather than rely on the organizer default.
2) Add the meeting time in the body with local times (e.g., "Nov 5, 16:00 JST / Nov 5, 15:00 SGT / Nov 5, 07:00 UTC").

Suggested corrected slot: Nov 5, 16:00 JST / 15:00 SGT. If that works for Mina, send the corrected invite and include an .ics that has Asia/Tokyo as the timezone.

Also: FYI, US DST ends Nov 2 this year — if Lauren is creating invites around that week from PDT/EDT machines, calendar clients sometimes flip the timezone anchor if the machine's settings are inconsistent. Not a Redwood-specific bug, but a recurring scheduling gotcha.

Hiro
Hiro Tanaka
Solutions Engineer (APAC) | Redwood Inference
hiro_tanaka@redwood.com
